Build a plan rule

Source: R/constraints.R
rules.Rd

Constructors for the rules a PlanConstraints holds, in the pattern of the op constructors: each returns the plain list you could write by hand – rule_min_share(0.4, target = list(channel = "Streaming")) is list(type = "min_share", value = 0.4, target = list(channel = "Streaming")) – and checks it where it is written.

Usage

rule_min_spend(value, target = NULL, during = NULL, note = NULL)

rule_max_spend(value, target = NULL, during = NULL, note = NULL)

rule_fixed_total(value, target = NULL, during = NULL, note = NULL)

rule_min_share(value, target = NULL, during = NULL, note = NULL)

rule_max_share(value, target = NULL, during = NULL, note = NULL)

rule_max_change_abs(value, target = NULL, during = NULL, note = NULL)

rule_max_change_pct(value, target = NULL, during = NULL, note = NULL)

Arguments

value

The rule's limit: an amount of money, or a share or fraction from 0 to 1 for the share rules (max_change_pct may exceed 1).

target

Optional named list of line item column = value(s), as in an op; omit for the whole plan. Rules measure whole days, so time is given by during, not by naming the time column.

during

Optional list(from =, to =) of dates.

note

Optional text saying why the rule exists.

Value

A plain list: one rule, for plan_constraints().

Details

Every rule measures the spend on its target rows inside its during window, day by day (as check_budget() does), and compares it with value:

rule_min_spend(), rule_max_spend()

That spend is at least, or at most, value.

rule_fixed_total()

That spend is exactly value – a commitment on a line's or a flight's total that leaves its phasing free. (A commitment month by month is a spend bound on the plan instead; see bound_cols().)

rule_min_share(), rule_max_share()

That spend, as a share of the whole plan's spend in the same window, is at least or at most value, from 0 to 1.

rule_max_change_abs(), rule_max_change_pct()

That spend moves by at most value – an amount, or a fraction of the reference's – from a reference plan, normally the parent or the current approved plan. check_constraints() needs the reference for these.

See also

plan_constraints(), check_constraints().

Examples

rule_min_share(0.4, target = list(channel = "Streaming"))
#> $type
#> [1] "min_share"
#> 
#> $value
#> [1] 0.4
#> 
#> $target
#> $target$channel
#> [1] "Streaming"
#> 
#> 
rule_max_change_pct(0.25, target = list(channel = "Online Video"),
                    note = "no channel swings more than 25%")
#> $type
#> [1] "max_change_pct"
#> 
#> $value
#> [1] 0.25
#> 
#> $target
#> $target$channel
#> [1] "Online Video"
#> 
#> 
#> $note
#> [1] "no channel swings more than 25%"
#>
